articles.body: Enzo Bardeli será baja en el partido de este próximo fin de semana ante la Real Sociedad, correspondiente a la jornada 10 de Primera División. El Levante ha emitido este mediodía un comunicado oficial anunciado la lesión muscular del mediocentro francés. articles.title: Carrick entona el mea culpa: "Hemos perdido un poco el rumbo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico del Manchester United admite el mal momento del equipo, califica de "inaceptable" la actuación del miércoles y reivindica los valores históricos del club en medio de los rumores sobre su futuro
articles.summary: El técnico del Manchester United admite el mal momento del equipo, califica de "inaceptable" la actuación del miércoles y reivindica los valores históricos del club en medio de los rumores sobre su futuro
articles.body: Michael Carrick atraviesa las horas más delicadas desde que asumió el mando del Manchester United. Con los resultados acumulando dudas y los rumores sobre posibles sustitutos creciendo en Inglaterra, el técnico compareció con un discurso cargado de autocrítica, responsabilidad y reivindicación de los valores históricos de Old Trafford. Lejos de buscar excusas, Carrick admitió que el equipo se ha alejado de la identidad que le permitió revertir la situación la pasada temporada y clasificarse para la Liga de Campeones. "Creo que últimamente no hemos pasado por un buen momento. Lo acepto totalmente. Tuvimos cinco meses de relativo éxito la temporada pasada, pero recientemente no hemos hecho las cosas lo suficientemente bien", reconoció, que además certifica que el vestuario no está dividido. Las palabras del entrenador llegan después de una serie de actuaciones muy cuestionadas, especialmente la del pasado miércoles, un encuentro que el propio técnico calificó de inadmisible. "Fue una mala noche por muchas razones. Me dolió mucho. Fue realmente inaceptable jugar así", confesó. Carrick colocó el foco sobre sí mismo y recordó cuál debe ser el nivel de exigencia de un club de la dimensión del United. "Mi responsabilidad es poner sobre el campo un equipo que represente a este club y a sus aficionados, uno del que puedan sentirse orgullosos", afirmó. Además, reconoció que el equipo se ha apartado de ese camino durante las últimas semanas. "Nos hemos desviado de eso en los partidos recientes. Soy plenamente consciente y estoy trabajando para corregirlo". El entrenador también lanzó un mensaje interno al recordar que nadie está por encima del club, incluido él mismo. "Manchester United siempre será más grande que cualquier individuo. Es más grande que yo y que cualquier jugador". Pese a la crudeza de sus declaraciones, el técnico no se mostró derrotado. Al contrario. Carrick insiste en que la situación es reversible y que aún confía en la capacidad de respuesta del equipo. "Hemos perdido un poco el rumbo, pero estoy convencido de que lo recuperaremos". Una declaración de intenciones en un momento en el que cada partido puede resultar decisivo para su continuidad al frente del banquillo de Old Trafford.

articles.title: Iñigo Pérez: “Soy de Pamplona y Aguirre era una referencia para mí cuando era niño”
articles.standfirst: El técnico amarillo espera que su equipo se reponga en Mestalla de la derrota en Anfield
articles.summary: El técnico amarillo espera que su equipo se reponga en Mestalla de la derrota en Anfield
articles.body: Iñigo Pérez considera que el derbi en Mestalla es la oportunidad perfecta para levantarse del golpe que supuso la derrota en Anfield. El técnico espera un parido “cerrado” toda vez que se refirió a Javier Aguirre como una referencia durante su niñez como técnico de Osasuna Como llegan los tocados: “La gestión de los dolores debe ser agudizada por el cuerpo técnico. Hay que ver como llegan algunos jugadores. Carlos Romero no estará en Valencia y Saliba ya veremos si puede jugar tras acabar con molestias en Liverpool” Derrota en Liverpool: “Toca hacer la revisión del partido en Liverpool y ser justo, tanto cuando el saldo es mayor como cuando es menor. La primera impresión es de rabia. Lo vimos en Dortmund o ante el Nápoles. Que cuando los equipos tienen su momento hacen daño al rival. En la primar parte la tuvimos muy clara y en los en la segunda. Pero en una fase que no fue abrumadora por su parte recibimos dos goles. Y eso te afecta anímicamente cuando llegas al descanso. Hay cosas positivas, pero tenemos que ceñirnos a aquello en lo que hay que mejorar y donde se nos escapó el partido”” Un derbi es diferente: “Nunca un derbi es un partido normal. Tiene componentes diferentes y se nota en el equipo y en los que le rodea. Es bonito venir de Anfield y tener la opción de jugar este partido en Mestalla. Es un punto al que agarrarte y cargarte de nievo de ilusión Más juego que puntos: “Creo que hemos demostrado más futbol que puntos, es uno de los análisis de lo que estoy seguro de que es así. Eso no quiere decir nada, pero hemos jugado muy bien durante algunos momentos y obtenido menos de lo que merecemos. En ese análisis está la respuesta: hacerlo mejor y tomar mejores decisiones para que caiga de nuestro lado Derbi que espera: “Es un partido en el que la emoción se nota ene l ambiente. Las realidades de cada equipo prevalecen. Espero un partido cerrado, medido. Tienen un técnico que ha jugado muchos derbis en otras regiones, y esa experiencia tratará de hacerla valer. No hay que salirse del guion que nos ha ido bien y esperar mayor acierto en las áreas” Poca distancia en la tabla: “Ya llevamos jornadas para que se vena los estratos de los jugadores, los niveles de los equipos. Es muy pronto para hablar de distancias entre sí, porque se trata de once meses largos y los dos últimos dos son donde se dan vuelcos. El partid de mañana es positivo para quien gane, pero no es definitivo pase lo que pase” Gestión de esfuerzos: “Algunos son medidos por la intensidad de los paridos y el volumen que estamos jugando, así como por lo internacionales. Es normal que haya cambios por esto y por las decisiones técnicas del entrenador” Valencia equipo intenso: “Sé de la capacidad de Aguirre para implementar la agresividad como rasgo de sus equipos y como una virtud. Nos conocemos, sabemos del ambiente y hay pocas cosas que te sorprendan. Pero cuando se juega los jugadores hacen suyo el encuentro” No ha perdido en Mestalla: “Ojalá siga, hay veces que te viene bien estas estadísticas pasadas. Ojalá podamos ganar porque el equipo viene de una dinámica buena, pero con el peor de los resultados. Todas las victorias son golpes en la mesa para e proceso de Iñigo o de cualquiera. las derrotas son un daño colateral, pero ganar sería importantísimo” Sobre Aguirre: “No recuerdo si me he medido con Aguirre, sé que yo estaba con Iraola cuando él estaba con Mallorca tengo pocas. Soy de Pamplona y lo veía de niño en Osasuna. Para mi Javier siempre ha sido una referencia, primero en mi infancia y luego cómo entrenador”

articles.title: Cleveland Browns News and Rumors 10/23/26: Scouting the Trap
articles.summary: CLEVELAND, OHIO (TheOBR.com) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans!THE DAILY BLOVIATIONTwo weeks ago, the Browns came off a walk-off win over the Steelers, f...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND, OHIO ( TheOBR.com ) - Good morning, Cleveland Browns fans!

Two weeks ago, the Browns came off a walk-off win over the Steelers, flew to New Jersey to play a one-win team in the rain, and lost 17-12. Fred Greetham's piece this morning is titled " Browns Must Learn the Lesson of the Jets Loss ." Chris Easterling calls the Titans " the ultimate trap opponent ." Jared Verse, for his part, doesn't believe in trap games. "Every team has a 'Dawg,'" he said.

My paranoia about all things, but particularly positive expectations about the Browns, has been well documented. Pick any random edition of this Massive Morning Missive, and you're sure to find something that will make you nod to yourself and say out loud, "Yep, he's paranoid." Also, "How much coffee does this guy drink ?" 27 years of this, my friends. 27 years. And the answer is "a lot."

So, it makes sense that I believe in trap games. I've watched this franchise step in more than a few. I'd also point out that the last time these teams met, last Dec. 7 in Cleveland, the Titans jumped out 14-3 in the first quarter, Tony Pollard ran for a career-high 161 yards, and Tennessee won 31-29 .

So before anybody pencils in 5-2, let's take a walk through Nashville.

THE INFIRMARY: This time of year, injury reports might be the best clue as to how a team is trending. The Titans are healthier than we are, which isn't saying much, because almost everybody is. Their Thursday injury report has seven names. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) went from limited Wednesday to not practicing Thursday. Pollard sat Thursday and Tyjae Spears sat Wednesday, both listed as rest. Safeties Kevin Winston Jr. (quad), who has missed the last two games, and Tony Adams (ankle) were limited both days. Linebacker Dorian Mausi is practicing fully on his way back from injured reserve. Ridley is also on the trade block, per Titans On SI , at a "career-low 13.5 receiving yards per game." So, factor that in accordingly.

Our list is longer. Quincy Williams missed Thursday with a neck injury, and Mike Rutenberg wouldn't say whether he'll play. Of all the weeks for that to happen, it's the one where Quincy faces Robert Saleh, his old head coach with the Jets. Carson Schwesinger, Grant Delpit and Elgton Jenkins came back as limited participants, per PFT , and Mason Graham is expected back . Friday's reports, with game statuses, come out this afternoon.

THE JORDAN ELLIOTT SITUATION: On Oct. 15, after an argument with left tackle JC Latham at practice, Elliott was sent off the field and went to his car in the players' lot to get his gun. Defensive lineman John Franklin-Myers talked him down. A source told NFL Network's Mike Garafolo the gun never left the parking spot. The Titans released Elliott on Tuesday, and Saleh confirmed the details Wednesday, calling it "a call for help more than a criminal act," per ESPN . The Titans notified the league, which is reviewing it, per the Tennessean .

On the field, the Titans lose a run-stopping tackle who followed Saleh from San Francisco, though he'd already been inactive for the Colts game. In Ask the Insiders, Tdfcpny is asking whether Elliott will ever play again . I don't know. He spent four years here after the Browns drafted him in the third round in 2020, and the football is the least important part of this one. I hope he gets the help he obviously needs.

THE TITANS OFFENSE: It's bad. The Titans are last in the league in total offense at 236.3 yards a game and tied for 31st in scoring at 14.0, per their own site . They're 32nd in time of possession at 24 minutes a game , 26th on third down and 29th in red zone touchdown rate, per Pro Football Reference . They beat the Colts while getting outgained 399-186 .

Two tendencies jump out. First, timing. Easterling found the Titans have played opponents even, 20-20, in the first quarter, then been outscored 62-3 in the second. The Browns have been outscored 44-6 in the first quarter, and the second is our best. The first quarter on Sunday could be interesting. Prepare to grimace, but know better times soon follow.

Second, the ball comes out fast and short. Cam Ward was sacked 55 times last year, tied for the league lead . This year the line has allowed only 10 sacks, but Ward has just 10 completions of 20-plus yards and one of 40-plus, per Titans On SI , which blames offensive coordinator Brian Daboll's "milquetoast scheme" about as much as the quarterback. Our defense has 19 sacks, second in the league. Something has to give there too.

CAM WARD: The first overall pick in 2025 is 4-19 as a starter, and AP notes he narrowly avoided becoming only the second quarterback of the common draft era to lose 20 of his first 23 starts. Per Pro Football Reference, the first was likely the world-famous Steve DeBerg.

Ward has 998 yards, four touchdowns, four interceptions and a 39.5 QBR, 29th in the league. Against the Colts he went 11-for-22 for 102 yards, his lowest total in any game he's finished. Saleh: "It's not all on the quarterback... But he is the face of the offense and he's got to play at a higher level." Ward: "We still know we are behind the eight-ball."

Todd Monken was kinder Wednesday. He said everyone tells him Ward is "there early, super diligent, highly competitive. That's a great starting point for a franchise quarterback." Cleveland is the last city on earth that should snicker at a young quarterback's rough second season. But I'd like our pass rush to make it rougher for one more Sunday.

CARNELL TATE: This is the Titan I've watched most, because he was a Buckeye. The fourth overall pick leads Tennessee with 29 catches for 344 yards in five games, and he caught his first NFL touchdown against the Colts, part of a six-catch, 70-yard day. Saleh is gushing : "He looked juicy right there... He just looked like a top five pick." Monken, who first met Tate when he visited Georgia as a recruit, said Wednesday that "he's wired like the guys we drafted." If I'm Rutenberg, Denzel Ward spends Sunday afternoon wherever Tate is.

THE DEFENSE: This is the realm of the Titans that can actually beat us, especially given the situation with the Browns' anemic running game. Saleh brought his attack-style front four, and Monken says they're "a lot like us." The centerpiece is Jeffery Simmons, the defensive tackle Ben Solak picked for Defensive Player of the Year through six weeks. He has four sacks and six tackles for loss , and he moves around the interior, so both our guards will see him, including rookie Austin Barber in his seventh NFL start. Tytus Howard faced Simmons nine times with Houston, and his advice was simple: "He has no weaknesses in his game... You have to bring it to him and don't back down... you just have to stand ten toes."

Against the Colts, Tennessee had six sacks and three takeaways. Simmons had two sacks and forced and recovered a fumble, and Jermaine Johnson II added two more sacks. This defense allows about 21.5 points a game, which isn't the reason the Titans are 1-5. The Browns' line has allowed a league-high 24 sacks. Not crazy about this matchup. If that offensive line is going to gel, now would be a really good time.

THE THIRD PHASE: John Fassel's special teams won the Colts game with a blocked punt returned for the go-ahead touchdown, a 58-yard Chimere Dike punt return and four Joey Slye field goals, including a 56-yarder. The Jets game turned on a special teams mistake too. Please hang on to the ball.

So that's the Titans. They can't move the ball, they play defense like they mean it, they block punts, and their best young player is a Buckeye getting better every week. That's the exact profile of a team that beats you 13-10 in a game you were supposed to win. They've also lost four straight at home, and they're desperate.

Verse is right that it isn't a trap game. It's just a game, and the Browns have to show up for the first quarter of it this time around. A good sign would be if they could prevent the Titans from scoring on their opening drive, which has been a challenge for the team all year.

QUICKLY: In Rams Watch, Puka Nacua left practice Thursday with a calf injury, with Davante Adams already out six to 10 weeks. And Cleveland lost a TV icon: Bob "Hoolihan" Wells died at 93 . If you grew up in Northeast Ohio, Friday nights belonged to Hoolihan and Big Chuck. Thanks for all of it.

Positive news from the world of sports and beyond...

Chemists at Osaka Metropolitan University made an aviation fuel from coconut fruit that gets thrown away during commercial oil extraction, using a process that runs at room temperature and below boiling instead of the high heat and pressure other biofuels need. Blended with kerosene and burned in a micro jet engine, it had thermal efficiency "comparable to that of pure kerosene" and cut unburned hydrocarbon emissions by 5 to 40 percent, depending on the blend. It also produces glycerin and biodiesel as byproducts, and the acetone and alcohol used in the process can be recovered. The researchers say it needs more work before it's ready for commercial use, mostly because of one downside: higher carbon monoxide emissions.

articles.title: Bukayo Saka injury ‘not good’ as Arsenal face nervous wait
articles.summary: Saka has not trained ahead of the Premier League clash against Everton
articles.body:
Arsenal are still yet to discover the extent of Bukayo Saka 's thigh injury but Mikel Arteta has admitted the early signs are "not good".

The England international pulled up with the issue in the first half of the 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich on Wednesday.

Saka is set to undergo further assessment ahead of Arsenal's home match against Everton on Saturday.

But he did not train on Friday and Arsenal face a nervous wait before discovering how long he could be sidelined for.

"He's got another MRI this afternoon because he had quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was difficult to understand the extent of the injury," Arteta said.

"We will know more probably tomorrow. We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists.

"Obviously when a player has to walk off the pitch and is struggling to walk without any pain and is restricted to movement, they are not good signs.

"So let's be very patient so we can give a definitive assessment, and then let you know."

Saka's injury means Noni Madueke and Eberechi Eze will have the opportunity to start against Everton.

Madueke scored Arsenal's winner at Nottingham Forest last Sunday while Eze was on target in the draw at the Allianz Arena in midweek.

With forward Christos Tzolis also sidelined, Madueke and Eze will be given additional responsibility for leading Arsenal's attack.

Saka missed several stretches of the past two seasons due to a mixture of muscle injuries - dealing with hamstring, thigh and hip problems.

The 25-year-old was also affected by an Achilles injury over the final stretch of last season, which impacted his fitness at the summer's World Cup.

Arsenal play five times before the November international break and travel to Liverpool in the Premier League next weekend.

Following Saturday's home game against Everton, there are also trips to Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup and Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

They conclude the stretch of fixtures by hosting Hull in the Premier League on 7 November ahead of the two-week international window.

articles.title: La amenaza fantasma
articles.standfirst: Gabriel Jesus ya sabe lo que es marcar al Real Madrid: tres goles con el City
articles.summary: Gabriel Jesus ya sabe lo que es marcar al Real Madrid: tres goles con el City
articles.body: Gabriel Jesus no necesita ser titular para convertirse en una amenaza. El delantero brasileño apunta a comenzar el Clásico desde el banquillo, pero Hansi Flick sabe que tiene en sus manos un recurso capaz de cambiar el partido en cualquier momento. Su capacidad para aparecer en los espacios, su movilidad y su olfato goleador le convierten en una alternativa de garantías para la segunda parte. Y hay un dato que invita a prestar atención: el Real Madrid se le da especialmente bien. El brasileño se ha enfrentado al conjunto blanco en cuatro ocasiones y ha marcado en tres de ellas. Una estadística que adquiere todavía más valor al observar los resultados: en los tres encuentros en los que vio portería, su equipo, el Manchester City, salió victorioso. En el único partido en el que no consiguió marcar, los ingleses acabaron perdiendo. Una curiosa coincidencia que alimenta su condición de futbolista capaz de hacer daño al Madrid cuando más importa. Ahora, Gabriel Jesus quiere trasladar esa amenaza al Barcelona. Su rendimiento en lo que va de temporada respalda su candidatura a convertirse en un revulsivo de lujo para Flick. El atacante suma cuatro goles en siete partidos disputados con el conjunto azulgrana, pese a haber sido titular únicamente en dos ocasiones. Unos números que reflejan su eficacia y su capacidad para aprovechar los minutos de los que dispone. Hay otro dato que explica su impacto: el brasileño firma un gol cada 58 minutos. Una media extraordinaria que demuestra que no necesita acumular demasiado tiempo sobre el césped para dejar su huella. Su presencia en el área, la facilidad para encontrar posiciones de remate y su intuición para detectar las debilidades defensivas le permiten ser una amenaza constante, incluso cuando entra con el partido avanzado. El escenario del Clásico parece hecho a medida para un futbolista de sus características. Con los defensas acumulando desgaste y los espacios creciendo a medida que pasan los minutos, Gabriel Jesus puede encontrar las condiciones ideales para explotar sus virtudes. Flick no parece reservarle un puesto en el once inicial, pero eso no significa que su papel vaya a ser secundario. La amenaza fantasma está preparada. Puede que el brasileño no aparezca desde el primer minuto, pero el Madrid tendrá que vigilarlo hasta el final. Porque sus antecedentes con el City, sus cifras y su eficacia invitan a pensar que, si tiene su oportunidad, puede volver a convertirse en protagonista.

articles.summary: Hall of Fame running back and Southern University coach Marshall Faulk has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease.
articles.body: Hall of Fame running back and Southern University coach Marshall Faulk has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease. Faulk revealed his diagnosis on the podcast “The Caring Neurologist” on Wednesday, telling the host, “I want to help as many people as I can.” The 53-year-old Faulk said he was not experiencing “issues” beyond hand rigidity and a few tremors, thanks to medication. He doesn’t believe the symptoms have gotten worse in the 18 months he’s been dealing with the disease. Faulk is in his first season as Southern’s coach after serving as running backs coach at Colorado. He played 12 NFL seasons with the Indianapolis Colts and St. Louis Rams, and was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2011.

articles.title: Dembele to miss Ballon d’Or event as PSG game moved amid protests in France
articles.summary: Paris Saint-Germain’s game has been postponed following a request by police amid a wave of violent protests in France.
articles.body:
Paris Saint-Germain’s home Ligue 1 game against Lyon scheduled for this Sunday has been postponed until Monday, the French league announced, following a request by police amid a wave of violent protests in the French capital.

The decision means the reigning Ballon d’Or, Ousmane Dembele, will miss Monday’s awards ceremony in London, for which he and a number of his PSG teammates have been nominated.

The 29-year-old French international forward was once again among the favourites to win the award, having helped his nation to the FIFA World Cup 2026 semifinals while leading PSG to their defence of the UEFA Champions League crown.

“The LFP takes note of the police decree prohibiting the staging of the game between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais on Sunday at 8:45 pm [19:45 GMT] … and has decided to reschedule the match for Monday at 8:30 pm,” the French league said in a statement on Friday.

French authorities are braced for another weekend of protests in Paris and across the country, after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago.

Defending champion PSG and Lyon were level on 14 points at the top of Ligue 1 heading into this weekend’s eighth round of games

Monday’s match will clash with the Ballon d’Or awards ceremony in London, where several PSG players are on the men’s shortlist: holder Dembele of France, Morocco’s Achraf Hakimi, Georgia’s Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Brazil’s Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves, and Vitinha of Portugal, Willian Pacho of Ecuador, and Fabian Ruiz and Ferran Torres of Spain.

French officials will mount a “massive” security operation for protests planned on Saturday, with troops reinforcing police, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said on Tuesday, after rioting and looting swept through Paris and other French cities on October 17.

The PSG-Lyon game is among several high-profile sporting events scheduled in the French capital area this weekend.

The Pittsburgh Steelers are due to face the New Orleans Saints in an NFL regular-season game at the Stade de France on Sunday, an event expected to require a significant police deployment.

Separately, Toulouse’s Ligue 1 home match against Troyes has already been pushed back from Saturday to Sunday at the request of local authorities, the LFP said on Wednesday.

articles.title: Bukayo Saka: Arsenal fear forward could be out for two months
articles.summary: Arsenal forward Bukayo Saka could be sidelined for up to eight weeks with the quadriceps injury he suffered against Bayern Munich.
articles.body:
Arsenal fear Bukayo Saka could miss a minimum of six weeks with the quadriceps injury he sustained in their Champions League tie against Bayern Munich.

The 25-year-old will undergo an MRI scan on Friday afternoon to better assess the problem, which forced him off in Wednesday's 2-2 draw at the Allianz Arena.

Fluid around the affected muscle has made diagnosing the injury difficult, but club medics are estimating, after early examinations, Saka will miss a minimum of six weeks and it could be even longer.

If those early concerns are realised, he will miss a clutch of key games for the Gunners, as well as England's forthcoming Uefa Nations League matches against Croatia and Spain.

"We need a few more scans and opinions from the specialists," said Arsenal head coach Mikel Arteta.

"When a player has to walk off the pitch, he is struggling to walk without any pain, and is restricted to movement; it is not a good sign. Let's be a little bit patient so we can give a definitive assessment.

"He's got another MRI as there was quite a lot of fluid in the area so it was quite difficult to understand the extent of the injury. We will know more tomorrow."

Saka will miss Saturday's home Premier League match against Everton , where second-placed Arsenal will hope to close a three-point gap on leaders Manchester City .

The Arsenal academy product has had fitness issues in recent months and his game time was managed at the end of last season, as well as with England at the World Cup, because of an Achilles injury he suffered in March.

He missed the March international break and seven games for the Gunners, but returned to help them lift the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years.

Saka started the Champions League final defeat by Paris St-Germain but was substituted after 54 minutes, and only started three of England's eight games at the World Cup - scoring a hat-trick in the 6-4 third-place win over France.

The forward also had surgery on a hamstring injury he picked up in December 2024, which kept him out for 101 days in the 2024-25 campaign.

He made 49 appearances as Arsenal won the title last term, despite a stop-start season. As well as the Achilles issue, Saka pulled out of a game in January against Leeds with a hip injury in the warm-up, while a hamstring problem also kept him out for about four weeks.

Question marks over Saka's robustness - analysis

The fact Saka needs follow-up scans and is likely to be out for up to eight weeks is a major blow for Arteta and Arsenal .

The Gunners boss had been speaking about how the player had been adapting his positioning to be more of a regular goalscorer for the club in recent weeks and the winger has scored four goals in 11 appearances so far this season.

But now Saka has gone down with another muscle injury there are questions about whether he still has the robustness that made him a certain starter in the Arsenal team.

The 25-year-old had Achilles, hip and hamstring problems last season and underwent surgery on a hamstring injury in the previous season which kept him out for 101 days.

He also had his game time managed at the World Cup in the summer with England and Arteta acknowledged Saka's robustness and availability has "certainly been different in the last year or so".

Arsenal tried to sign a world-class forward to level up their frontline in the summer but were unable to do so, with unsuccessful pursuits of Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez.

They did bring in Greece international Christos Tzolis, but he is currently injured too.

That has left them with Noni Madueke, Eberechi Eze and 16-year-old Max Dowman as alternative wing options.

Teenager Dowman has had limited minutes this season but Arteta spoke glowingly of his talent and ability to impact matches.

articles.title: Nicolas Raskin happy at Rangers but unsure about possibility of January move or new contract
articles.summary: Belgium midfielder Nicolas Raskin is "really happy" at Rangers but is unsure what might happen in January.
articles.body:
Nicolas Raskin is "really happy" at Rangers but unsure about what might happen in January.

The Belgium midfielder, 25, scored his first goal of the season in last weekend's 2-2 draw at Dundee, having started Rangers' past seven games.

He had been linked with a move away in the summer and was left out of some games amid a possible move.

Since joining Rangers in January 2023, the midfielder has made more than 150 club appearances and picked up 22 Belgium caps.

"It wasn't that difficult," said Raskin when asked about refocusing on Rangers after the World Cup and transfer uncertainty.

"The hardest was not being able to play. Watching the boys playing, this is probably the hardest bit I've been through during the window.

"When you're an ambitious player, you want to keep going higher and higher and higher. I thought there was a point where maybe I could try and go and get for a new challenge after the World Cup.

"I've never been pushing for something because I'm really happy here. It's a big club. This club helped me join the Belgian national team, which is a big, big thing.

"I'm really calm with that. I don't need to push anything. The manager's been amazing with me since he arrived. We've got loads of time before January. We try to make the best of it, try to win as many games as we can and I don't know what's going to happen."

Asked about the possibility of extending his contract before the end of next season, the Belgian added: "I don't know, it's not up to me. It's up to the club."

Manager Derek McInnes said of Raskin: "We're not looking to lose players in January and Nico's been a key player for us and hopefully he's a key player in a successful Rangers team this season.

"January's not a window you want to be losing key players. Clubs can bid above and beyond what a player's value is.

"If there was an opportunity to work with Nico beyond [his current deal] then obviously it's something that I would not be against.

"Nico said to me that he could've had one or two things that he could've jumped at in the end of the transfer window but he's keen to be here and be part of a successful team.

"Unless something comes up that really turns his head and really turns Rangers' head, then we keep working together."

Meanwhile, McInnes revealed a sickness bug has affected his squad and may make two of his regular starters doubtful for Saturday's visit of Scottish Premiership opponents St Johnstone.

articles.title: Carrick accepts blame for Man United slump, but ‘confident’ of a turnaround
articles.summary: Manchester United make worst start to a season in 40 years, but Michael Carrick ‘confident’ ahead of Bournemouth game.
articles.body:
Manchester United manager Michael Carrick mounted an impassioned defence of ⁠⁠his leadership on Friday, accepting responsibility ⁠⁠for the club’s collapse in form and saying he remains convinced he can lead the team out of their current crisis.

Carrick’s position is under increasing pressure after United extended their winless run to seven matches in all competitions with Wednesday’s humiliating 4-1 ⁠⁠Champions League defeat at Como leaving them 20th in the table with three points.

Before taking questions ahead of Sunday’s Premier League home game against Bournemouth, Carrick delivered an emotional opening statement, acknowledging supporters’ frustrations and the scale of the challenge facing him.

“Recently, we haven’t had a good time. I think that’s ⁠⁠pretty obvious. So I totally accept what we’re going through at the moment,” he said.

“We had five months of relative success [last season] in a spell where I was happy with a lot of things I was seeing and that we were doing as a team,” he said.

“We haven’t done well enough lately. We’ve had a spell that we’re really not happy with.”

Carrick described the loss in Italy as one of the most painful nights of his tenure.

“Wednesday was a bad ‌‌night. It was a bad night for a lot of reasons. It hurt a lot,” he said. “It obviously hurt me to see us play that way. As I said after the game, it was really unacceptable.”

The defeat intensified scrutiny of Carrick after captain Bruno Fernandes appeared to question United’s tactical approach in his post-match comments.

Dressing room cracks for Carrick after Fernandes outburst

Asked whether public criticism from players suggested cracks within the dressing room, Carrick rejected any suggestion the squad was split.

He also sidestepped questions over Fernandes’ future as captain and declined to reveal whether he had held talks with the Portugal midfielder following the defeat.

Instead, he stressed that his priority was restoring an identity that has disappeared from the side in recent weeks.

“My responsibility is to ⁠⁠get a team on the pitch that represents this football club, represents the supporters and they can be proud ⁠⁠of it with the identity that we show,” Carrick said.

“We have gone away from that just recently in certain games, which I’m fully aware of and definitely doing something about.”

He reserved special mention for United’s fans, many of whom travelled to Como only to watch their side suffer the heaviest defeat of his reign.

“The supporters are a huge part of this ⁠⁠football club. They have to make the effort and the time and money they spend, to feel how we all felt on Wednesday was a tough moment,” he said.

Carrick defiant as Man United form slides

Despite growing speculation about his future, Carrick struck a ⁠⁠defiant tone, saying he remained confident United could rediscover the energy and connection that characterised ⁠⁠last season’s performances.

He took over in January 2026 after the sacking of Ruben Amorim and oversaw a remarkable turnaround, steering United to a top-three finish and Champions League qualification.

“For [the fans] to feel like they felt for five months at the start of the year … is something we need to get back to. We will get back to it. I fully believe that,” said ‌‌Carrick.

Former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager Antonio Conte is among the names linked with United’s managerial job, although the 57-year-old Italian said on Friday he had not had any negotiations “at an advanced stage” with any club.

Carrick acknowledged that United had lost their way but said responsibility rested squarely with him.

He ended ‌‌his ‌‌opening remarks by saying it was his duty to get the club back on course, describing his role as “holding the umbrella for me to get wet and everyone else to stay dry”.

United are 13th in the Premier League standings on seven points, while Bournemouth are a point behind them in 15th.

articles.title: Cristiano se queda a cero: le 'quitan' el 0-2, le anulan otro y remata al poste
articles.standfirst: El tanto 982 del luso queda a la espera
articles.summary: El tanto 982 del luso queda a la espera
articles.body: No falló Al Nassr en su visita a Harmah... pero sí hubo lío con el 'gol fantasma' de Cristiano Ronaldo. Los de Postecoglou ganaron 1-3 con un Cristiano Ronaldo omnipresente que sin embargo, a instancias de OPTA y otras fuentes estadísticas, se quedó sin marcar. El portugués, que 'hizo' el 0-2 (hubiera sido su gol número 982), también tuvo otro tanto anulado y un remate al poste, además de ver cómo Pacheco evitaba su gol en otra serie de acciones. Ese gol, no obstante, OPTA se lo dio a Andrei Girotto en propia puerta... al finalizar el partido. La liga saudí y Al Nassr, no obstante, lo mantienen como autor. Pese al buen gol de Al Hamdan a los cuatro minutos, con un disparo colocado desde la frontal, a Al Nassr le cuesta más ganar este curso con Postecoglou que en la 2025-26 bajo el mando de Jorge Jesus, cuando fue campeón. Al Faysaly apretó a un equipo, el de CR7, que tardó en sacar su mejor fútbol. El de Madeira, de hecho, apenas apareció en el primer tiempo. La más clara llegó pasada la media hora, a pase de Joao Félix, con un disparo cruzado que se topó con la madera. Fue sin embargo, ya en la segunda parte, cuando Al Nassr se 'soltó'. Y empezó a brillar Cristiano Ronaldo. El astro luso propició el 0-2 con un gran cabezazo a centro medido de Joao Félix, en una falta lateral. OPTA, sin embargo, entiende que el que toca es Girotto aunque la liga saudí se lo daba a CR7. Era el 0-2. Tres minutos después hizo el tercero al contragolpe... pero el VAR revisó la acción y rectificó el tanto por fuera de juego previo de Al Hamdan. Los locales tuvieron su momento tras la entrada al campo del español Jaime Seoane y el ex Celta Theo Bongonda. Fue el belga, precisamente, el que en una jugada aislada puso el 1-2 en un remate de cabeza. Pero Al Nassr había tomado el 'tempo' al encuentro y el partido no se le iba a escapar. Fernando Pacheco, meta en el equipo de Harmah, le sacó una gran mano a CR7 cuando el luso buscaba el tercero del partido... y fue Angelo finalmente, tras una buena jugada colectiva, el que sentenció después del 'cooling break'. Al Nassr, mientras, iguala en cabeza con este triunfo a Al Qadsiah... a la espera de que el equipo de Brendan Rodgers se mida esta noche a Al Hilal, que marcha en estos momentos tercero.

articles.title: Mourinho apaga los incendios del vestuario
articles.standfirst: Los pesos pesados de la plantilla están encantados con la cercanía del portugués y su manera de gestionar el grupo, tras una etapa marcada por los desencuentros internos
articles.summary: Los pesos pesados de la plantilla están encantados con la cercanía del portugués y su manera de gestionar el grupo, tras una etapa marcada por los desencuentros internos
articles.body: En Valdebebas empieza a instalarse una tranquilidad en el vestuario blanco que hacía tiempo que no se respiraba. Mourinho está consiguiendo conectar con los jugadores con más peso de la plantilla... y todos valoran especialmente su cercanía y su manera de gestionar las relaciones dentro del grupo. "Están muy contentos con él. Es un tío muy cercano", apuntan desde dentro del búnker blanco. El respeto que despierta el portugués por su trayectoria es indiscutible, pero hay algo más que está marcando la diferencia en el día a día. Mourinho se queda con los futbolistas después de los entrenamientos, bromea con ellos y sabe cómo tratar a cada uno en función de su personalidad. Una cercanía que está ayudando a generar una conexión especial con el grupo. "Sabe manejar muy bien los egos y cómo es cada jugador", cuentan desde la Ciudad Real Madrid.. El cambio cobra especial relevancia por lo vivido anteriormente. Las etapas de Xabi Alonso y Arbeloa estuvieron marcadas por distintos desencuentros con miembros de la plantilla, con frentes abiertos que terminaron generando distancias entre el cuerpo técnico y algunos futbolistas. El vestuario llegó a convivir con diferentes sensibilidades, entre aliados y detractores, en un escenario que complicaba la gestión del grupo. Ahora, el mensaje que llega desde dentro apunta en otra dirección. Los jugadores de mayor peso están satisfechos con el trato recibido y con una gestión que combina autoridad, experiencia y cercanía. Mourinho no solo está encontrando la manera de llegar a los futbolistas, sino también de ganarse su confianza. Más allá de los resultados, el portugués parece haber encontrado la fórmula para rebajar las tensiones y recuperar la sintonía con los referentes del vestuario. Algo que al arrancar el curso se marcó como prioritario para empezar a encajar todas las piezas. En un equipo en el que los problemas de convivencia habían condicionado etapas anteriores, la sensación que se transmite ahora desde Valdebebas es la de un grupo más cómodo con su entrenador y una relación más fluida entre el cuerpo técnico y sus futbolistas.

articles.summary: El técnico espera que el Racing recupere su mejor versión ante el Espanyol
articles.body: José Alberto, entrenador del Racing, tiene claro que su equipo debe mejorar para olvidar los últimos malos resultados cosechados en el campeonato. "Tenemos que dar un paso adelante en todas las fases del juego, en gestionar cada momento y la entrada a los partidos. Estamos trabajando para ser un equipo más fiable a nivel ofensivo y defensivo", comentó. El técnico racinguista avisaba sobre el peligro del Espanyol: "Nuestro rival tiene a Roberto que vive un momento impresionante, además de jugadores internacionales y con experiencia en Primera. Es un equipo físico, intenso, con velocidad y jerarquía atrás. Les hemos estudiado bien y conocemos sus virtudes y sus debilidades". Sobre la lucha por la salvación, José Alberto tiene claro que será una pugna dura: "Veo grandes rivales por la permanencia y todos tienen buenos recursos para ganar partidos. Vamos a luchar por conseguirla".

articles.title: Vincent Kompany: Bayern Munich boss taken to hospital after collapsing at training ground
articles.summary: Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany was taken to hospital after collapsing at the club's training ground on Friday; the Belgian's condition is said to be stable, according to Sky in Germany
articles.body:
Kompany's condition is said to be stable, according to Sky in Germany .

"Vincent Kompany had to seek medical treatment on Friday after collapsing during training for FC Bayern's amateurs," said the club in a statement.

"The first-team coach had been watching the second team's session. Kompany will undergo thorough examination in the hospital and remain in medical care. For the time being, his coaching staff will manage training and match operations."

Director of sport Max Eberl added: "Vincent Kompany's health is our top priority. We at FC Bayern will do everything we can to ensure he makes a speedy recovery.

"Vinnie is receiving all the necessary medical care and support, and all the time he needs. His coaching team, in whom we have complete confidence, will take over his duties. All of us at FC Bayern wish Vinnie a speedy recovery."

Kompany's former club Manchester City also sent their best wishes, with a post on their X feed reading: "Everyone at Manchester City is wishing a speedy recovery to our former captain and club legend, Vincent Kompany.

The Bayern head coach has been suffering from a viral infection of late and was unable to attend his side's pre-match presser ahead of the midweek Champions League game against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena.

Kompany was well enough to take his place in the dugout though for the 2-2 draw against the Gunners on Wednesday.

Bayern face Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

articles.title: Steve Sarkisian, Texas Used New AI Platform 'Bevo Lab' for Crucial 4th Down Decision vs. Florida
articles.summary: University of Texas head football coach Steve Sarkisian's decision to go for it on a fourth-and-2 during the fourth quarter of last weekend's 27-24 loss to Florida was aided by artificial intelligence.
articles.body:
University of Texas head football coach Steve Sarkisian's decision to go for it on a fourth-and-2 during the fourth quarter of last weekend's 27-24 loss to Florida was aided by artificial intelligence.

Texas athletic director Chris Del Conte divulged that information in an interview with Karoline Leonard of the Austin American-Statesman this week, noting that Texas' Bevo Lab AI platform is "the new wave."

The decision to go for it came with Texas trailing 20-17 and positioned at its own 48-yard line with just over 8:30 remaining in the game.

Texas quarterback Arch Manning tried to run up the middle after stepping back to pass, but he was stopped for a loss, and Florida scored a touchdown six plays later to extend the lead to 10.

Per Leonard, Bevo Lab will be available to coaches, trainers, nutritionists, student-athletes and analysts for every Longhorns sports team.

The platform is sponsored by Dell, Google and SHI International, and it will use Google's Cloud Platform and Gemini agentic AI system.

Del Conte called the development "earth-shattering," while UT Business Sports Institute founder Kirk Goldsberry added, "We're trying to put good data and good intelligence in front of our coaches, so that they can make informed decisions and informed strategies to help us ultimately win more competitions at The University of Texas."

Although Bevo Lab made its debut last week with the football team, every varsity sport at the University of Texas will soon have access to the platform.

Following a 4-0 start, which included wins over ranked opponents in Ohio State and Tennessee, Texas is now 4-2 on the heels of back-to-back losses to Oklahoma and Florida.

Now, the Longhorns are perhaps entering a must-win scenario on Saturday against No. 7 Ole Miss.

Should No. 19 Texas lose, it could virtually mark the end of the Longhorns' pursuit of a College Football Playoff berth.

The use of Bevo Lab did not prevent a loss to Florida last week, but Del Conte's comments suggest it will not prevent the coaching staff from utilizing AI this week against the Rebels.

articles.title: Johannes Spors: Southampton technical director on Spygate scandal
articles.summary: Southampton group technical director Johannes Spors says that the Spygate scandal put him in a "difficult position" over the summer.
articles.body:
Southampton group technical director Johannes Spors says the Spygate scandal put him in a "difficult position" over the summer as the club were preparing for the new season.

In May, Saints were kicked out of the play-offs and deducted four points for admitting they spied on three clubs during the Championship season.

The future of head coach Tonda Eckert was then put into question as a Football Association (FA) investigation took place that could have seen the German coach handed a ban that might have cost him his job.

As the season commenced, the club and their supporters did not know if Eckert would be handed a personal sanction for his role in the scandal, but in early October those fears were put to rest when the FA announced he would be fined £28,000 and that a six-week ban would be suspended until the end of next season.

Saints could have sacked Eckert after he admitted to his mistakes in May, but decided to stick with their man as owner Dragan Solak and the rest of the board gave him a second chance.

"Of course, it did put me into a difficult position," Spors told BBC Radio Solent.

"It was something that probably no-one, or at least not many sporting directors have experienced, planning into a season and a squad with that level of uncertainty.

"I only felt one choice and I'm happy that everybody around me, including Dragan Solak, was very aligned.

"We decided to go this route (backing Eckert) and take it with all consequences and I'm happy we've done that."

Follow Southampton content on BBC Sounds

Pre-match, post-match and topical Saints content

Spors was appointed Southampton's group technical director in February 2025 and played a key role in the appointment of Eckert.

He has previously held six sporting director roles at clubs including Belgian Pro League team Standard Liege and Serie A side Genoa.

While the Spygate saga rumbled on over the summer, Spors revealed that he felt an obligation to support Eckert on a personal level.

"That was something I really focused a lot in the summer, to support him as much as I could," he added.

"We cannot forget that he's a young man with a lot going on in his life, coming into a new country as an unknown and being on the highest level of recognition pretty quickly.

"I just wanted to make sure that he's OK as a human being. I helped him with everything I can with my knowledge, my expertise, but also my friendship.

"I made sure that there are even more people around him who helped him, who have more expertise in certain things than I have and are specialists in areas that he needed help and support over the whole summer."

'It's changed my life' - Eckert on Spygate scandal

Eckert free to stay as Southampton boss as Spygate ban suspended

Southampton expelled from play-offs for spying

Saints have started the Championship season well and sit eighth in the table after 11 matches.

They have the best home record in the league, unbeaten with five wins and one draw at St Mary's.

On matchdays, Spors can be seen in the directors' box alongside chief executive Phil Parsons and other members of the club's board.

He felt that it was not a difficult choice to personally back Eckert and keep him at the club over the summer.

"We have known each other for nearly 10 years," he said.

"We worked in Italy and at Red Bull together so I developed a lot of parts of his career, the pro licence, and then the signing here to Southampton.

"I was just convinced that he is a very good manager, there's always a little bit of risk that how does it really work in the reality, but I was super convinced that he would be the right choice.

"Our relationship is close, we speak to each other nearly every day and support each other, we can also have hard discussions behind closed doors, where we challenge each other and I think that's as important as the support."

articles.title: Yamal, Mbappe in El Clasico spotlight as 40 cameras dedicated to coverage
articles.summary: The coverage includes ultra-high-definition filming, slow-motion replays, and individual player tracking techniques.
articles.body:
Sunday’s highly anticipated El Clasico will see up to 40 cameras cover the match between Barcelona and Real Madrid, including dedicated coverage of stars Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe a day before Ballon d’Or winners are announced.

The cameras will be placed across Camp Nou Stadium as part of a television production plan that includes ultra-high-definition filming, slow-motion replays, and individual player tracking techniques, Spanish newspaper Mundo Deportivo reported on Tuesday.

Spain’s top-flight La Liga classifies matches involving Barcelona or Real Madrid as “Category A”, requiring at least 22 cameras for coverage.

Major matches like El Clasico or the Madrid Derby have a higher rating of “A+” and require 35 to 40 cameras distributed according to a pre-defined shooting plan, which includes their locations and coverage angles.

The details are made available to the referees’ technical committee and the Video Assistant Referee (VAR) technology team, advising them of the available image sources for reviewing refereeing decisions.

The announcement of expanded coverage follows controversy in the Real Madrid vs Sevilla match on Sunday, which saw an off-the-ball clash with Real Madrid midfielder Adra Guler and Sevilla’s Peque Fernandez in the 24th minute.

Despite 26 cameras being used during the match, none of the available angles provided a clear enough picture to determine the nature of the contact between the players, thereby reviving the debate on whether television coverage can provide the angles required to decide in controversial cases.

However, using more cameras does not guarantee that all events will be clearly filmed; it depends on the location of the equipment, direction of the lenses, and how close the event is to the angle being filmed by the camera.

Anticipated coverage includes cameras with long-range and cinematic lenses, with the production of images in “4K” resolution compared to “full HD”.

This allows the television director to choose between multiple angles during the game, and replay important shots in clearer detail, especially goals, dangerous opportunities, and collisions inside the penalty areas.

Additionally, cameras will be installed behind the two goals, as well as equipment capable of capturing fast shots and replaying them in slow motion.

Is this the first time camera innovation has been enabled?

During a 2017 El Clasico, the Spanish League used 40 cameras mounted on cranes and carried by helicopters, as well as slow-motion cameras dedicated to tracking Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. More than 400 specialists in photography, directing and television production were involved.

In 2016, El Clasico experimented with 360-degree replays using a system based on cameras distributed around the stadium to produce three-dimensional images, allowing the director to show some scenes from virtual angles that are difficult to obtain using a traditional camera.

The league later developed this technology through a system that uses images captured by 38 high-resolution cameras to produce stereoscopic scenes, allowing the viewer to see the shooting angle from a virtual location close to the player.

In newer versions, coverage has reached 32, 34 and 38 cameras depending on the stadium and match conditions, with the introduction of cinematography, aerial cameras, drones, visual effects and live data.
